- I study for tests the way I charge my phone: wait until 2% and then panic.
- Multiple choice strategy: When in doubt, pick C. When not in doubt… still pick C.
- My teacher said it’s a no-calculator test. Great, so we’re doing history, because we’re going back in time.
- Pop quiz: Did you read the chapter? A) Yes B) No C) I’ll pick C
- I love open-book tests. It’s like the exam saying, “I know you don’t remember any of this.”
- Scantrons: the adult coloring book that judges you.
- My code passes all unit tests—unfortunately, the users weren’t included in the test suite.
- Integration tests: where your bugs meet my bugs and start a family.
- End-to-end tests are just pressing a button and whispering, “Please work.”
- QA told me my feature was unstable. I said it’s not a bug, it’s a surprise mechanic. QA said the surprise is the crash.
- Test anxiety is when your smartwatch thinks you’re doing cardio while sitting.
- Grading curve: because nothing says “fair” like everyone being wrong together.
